idea.body: A polynomial's factored form shows its zeros directly. In P(x) = (x - 2)^3(x + 1)^2, the graph crosses the x-axis at x = 2 and touches it at x = -1. An odd power crosses the axis, and an even power only touches it. The degree is the sum of all the powers. It bounds the turning points at one less than the degree. Together with the sign of the leading coefficient, it also gives the end behavior. A positive leading coefficient on an even degree sends both ends up; an odd degree sends the ends in opposite directions. For P(x) = (x - 2)^3(x + 1)^2, the degree is 5, so the graph falls on the left and rises on the right.

figure.alt: The graph of (x - 2)^3(x + 1)^2, crossing at x = 2 and touching at x = -1.

workedExample.prompt: P(x) = -(x + 3)(x - 1)^2(x - 4). Describe the end behavior and what happens at each zero.
steps: The zeros are x = -3 (multiplicity 1, crosses), x = 1 (multiplicity 2, touches), and x = 4 (multiplicity 1, crosses).
The degree is 1 + 2 + 1 = 4, an even number.
The leading coefficient is -1, since multiplying out the factors' leading terms gives -x^4.
An even degree with a negative leading coefficient falls on both the left and the right.

figure.alt: The graph of -(x + 3)(x - 1)^2(x - 4) near x = 1, touching the axis there without crossing. The zeros at x = -3 and x = 4 lie outside this window.

ways.name: The sign chart
ways.when: when you want to see where P(x) is positive or negative.
steps: Plot every zero of P(x) on a number line.
Test one point in each interval between zeros.
Record plus or minus for each interval based on that test point.
Read the pattern off the chart to sketch the graph.
ways.trap: Testing at a zero instead of strictly between zeros, which gives 0, not a sign.

figure.alt: A sign chart for (x - 1)(x + 2)(x - 3): zeros marked at -2, 1 and 3 on a number line, with minus, plus, minus, plus written in the four intervals.

frames.caption: Plot every zero of P(x) on a number line.

Record plus or minus for each interval.
Read the pattern to sketch the graph.

ways.name: End behavior from the leading term
ways.when: when you need to know which way the graph goes as x grows large.
steps: The degree tells you even or odd.
The leading coefficient tells you positive or negative.
Even degree, positive lead: both ends up.
Odd degree, positive lead: left down, right up.
ways.answer: Degree 4 (even), leading coefficient -2 (negative). Both ends fall.
ways.trap: Ignoring the sign of the leading coefficient, or getting the degree wrong.

ways.name: The rational root list
ways.when: when you search for possible rational zeros before graphing.
steps: List factors of the constant term.
List factors of the leading coefficient.
Every ratio (factor of constant) / (factor of leading) is a candidate.
Test each with the remainder theorem to find actual roots.
ways.trap: Forgetting the plus or minus, or including the leading coefficient in the numerator.

ways.name: Sum and product of roots
ways.when: when you know the roots exist but do not know them individually.
steps: For ax^2 + bx + c, the sum of roots is -b/a.
The product of roots is c/a.
These values constrain what the roots can be.
Useful to check if a factorization is correct.
ways.trap: Forgetting to divide by a, or getting the sign of the sum wrong.
